nadia.park: Hi team — quick onboarding question. Im going to be working remotely from the UK until I relocate to the US in July. Offer start date is 2026-05-01. How do we handle Form I-9 since Im not physically in the US? Can the US embassy/consulate notarize my passport and that count for Section 2? Also who covers notary/courier fees if needed?

tom.peopleops: Good q. Short version: Form I-9 Section 2 generally requires physical inspection of original documents by the employer (or an authorized representative) within 3 business days of hire. If you're physically outside the US at hire, we usually defer the I-9 until you are physically present in the US. There are two options we can consider:

  1) Defer I-9 until youre in the US and set your hire date accordingly (or set a remote start but pause payroll until docs are provided).
  2) Use an authorized representative in the UK (a notary/consular official) to inspect originals and complete Section 2 on our behalf, but this requires pre-approval from Legal/People Ops.

For the embassy notarization question: a US consulate/embassy notarization is commonly used, but the person who signs Section 2 must be willing to sign as our authorized representative and include their title and contact info.

erin.legal: Adding to Tom: legally the employer remains responsible for the integrity of Section 2 even if an authorized representative performs the inspection. If we go the "authorized representative" route, we need:
  - pre-approval from Legal (I can review the rep wording)
  - an explicit statement from the rep that they examined originals
  - a scanned copy of Section 2 with the reps signature + contact details
  - the employee to courier the originals or notarized copies to HR within a short window (we typically ask for originals or certified copies within 10 business days)

Note: the "remote verification" flex that existed during pandemic is not a guaranteed legal safe harbor today, so pre-approval is required. Also we should evaluate tax/residency implications if you perform work for Redwood from the UK prior to US arrival.

josh.payroll: From payroll: we can provision an employee record with the planned start date. However we cannot release payroll until Section 2 is complete and we have proof of authorization to work. If you prefer to start on 2026-05-01 but delay pay, we can do that (youd sign an agreement acknowledging pay hold). Alternatively we set a US effective hire date when you arrive and then run a retroactive payroll if youre owed back pay once docs are in.

carla-onboarding: Practical checklist if you want to pursue the consular/notary route (please use secure upload for scans, do NOT Slack originals):
  - Upload to onboarding portal: passport bio page (original), visa stamp (if applicable), current UK address, offer letter.
  - Arrange an appointment at the US consulate or a UK notary who agrees to act as an authorized representative; get them to confirm they will complete Form I-9 Section 2 and include contact info.
  - We require the rep to complete Section 2, sign, and add a scanned copy to the portal.
  - Courier instructions: send originals or certified copies to People Ops at our SF office within 10 business days. We will reimburse reasonable courier/notary fees (please keep receipts; reimbursement cap $75 unless pre-approved).

Ill DM you a template wording for the authorized representative to use when signing Section 2 so Legal has consistent language.

onboarding-bot: Reminder: do NOT post passport or SSN scans in Slack. Use the secure onboarding portal. See onboarding.redwood.com/upload.

nadia.park: Thanks everyone  that helps a ton. Ill set the consulate appointment and upload docs. Id like to keep 2026-05-01 as my start but am OK signing the pay-hold acknowledgement if needed. Carla: please send the template and cost-reimbursement steps. Erin: Id appreciate any tax residency flags to watch for.

tom.peopleops: Sounds good. Carla will send templates; Erin will flag any tax notes after a quick review. Well mark this thread and follow up once we have the consulate confirmation. :thumbsup:
